key_insight: Encoding structural modes in few qubits is not enough: reliable variational quantum modal analysis also requires controlled deflation, expressive circuits, and substantial measurement resources.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers assess quantum modal-analysis accuracy and resource costs for structural dynamics and damage localization without assuming a computational speedup.
method: Use Cholesky whitening to align quantum-state orthogonality with structural mass orthogonality.
Derive a necessary-and-sufficient deflation penalty threshold and bound approximate-projector effects.
Evaluate mapping, circuit expressibility, preprocessing, Pauli growth, shot uncertainty, and damage localization separately.
evidence_signal: For 128-DOF chains, consistent-mass whitening increased Pauli terms from 576 to 2,950; first-mode frequency RMS error was 2.45% at 100,000 shots per term, and an oracle-state study localized 10% stiffness loss in 84.5% of trials.
watch_item: Whitening and measurement costs can offset compact qubit encoding; oracle-state localization results do not establish end-to-end hardware performance or quantum speedup.
paper_title: Qubits Are Not Enough: Deflation and Measurement Limits in Variational Quantum Modal Analysis
